If $\gcd(m,n)=1$, then
\[
|(g,h)|=\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)=mn.
\]
Hence $(g,h)$ has order equal to the order of the whole group and generates $G_1\times G_2$. Thus the product is cyclic.

Conversely, suppose that $G_1\times G_2$ is cyclic. Then some element $(x,y)$ has order $mn$. Since $x\in G_1$ and $y\in G_2$, their orders divide $m$ and $n$, respectively. Therefore
\[
|(x,y)|=\operatorname{lcm}(|x|,|y|)\mid \operatorname{lcm}(m,n).
\]
It follows that $mn\leq \operatorname{lcm}(m,n)$. On the other hand, $\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)\mid mn$, so equality holds. The identity
\[
\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)=\frac{mn}{\gcd(m,n)}
\]
then gives $\gcd(m,n)=1$.

Therefore $G_1\times G_2$ is cyclic if and only if $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime.
\end{proof}
